title: An unparsed value prints `-0` as `0`, so a division by it flips the sign of its infinity
impact: Agent-style spec report, no real project or reactions. Only observable when a literal -0 ends up as a divisor (or in sign()) inside a calc kept as tokens, i.e. `calc(1px / -0)`-style input nobody writes.
code: src/properties/custom.rs: TokenList::to_css, Token::Number via CSSNumber::to_css zero branch -> cssparser `ToCss for f32` prints -0.0 as `0`
summary: Number tokens `-0` in unparsed values (var() fallbacks, custom properties, calcs that fail to parse) print as `0`. Per the css-values-4 Editor's Draft, a literal `-0` already produces unsigned (positive) zero, so `calc(1px / -0)` and `calc(1px / 0)` are the same value and the minified output is equivalent per spec. Chromium and WPT disagree: they treat a literal -0 as negative zero, so in Chromium the output differs (only for this absurd input). The minifier already normalizes number tokens in custom properties (`+1` -> `1`, `1.0` -> `1`).
repro: triage/sweep/1398-repro.mjs (controls only: negative non-zero signs kept, -0 prints as a zero). `.a{margin-left:calc(1px / (-0 * var(--z)))} .b{margin-left:var(--y, calc(1px / -0))} .c{--x:calc(1px / -0)}` -> `.a{margin-left:calc(1px / (0 * var(--z)))}.b{margin-left:var(--y,calc(1px / 0))}.c{--x:calc(1px / 0)}` on master and the latest 3 releases. Also `width:calc(1px / -0)` (unparsed because of #1399) -> `calc(1px / 0)`, and `--x:-0` -> `--x:0`.
evidence: repro.mjs on local (= master), 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1: identical. Spec css-values-4 Overview.bs #calc-ieee: "Signed zeros (indicated here as 0⁺ or 0⁻) can not be written directly in CSS; ''0'', ''+0'' and ''-0'' all produce the standard \"unsigned\" zero, which is considered positive (0⁺)". So the reporter's premise ("a negative zero keeps its sign") contradicts the ED. However WPT css/css-values/signed-zero.html expects `calc(-0)` to be negative, and Chromium 153 computes `margin-left: calc(1px / -0)` = -3.35544e+07px and `calc(1px / (-0 * var(--z)))` = -3.35544e+07px, i.e. spec and implementations/tests disagree. Open CSSWG issues #7472 ('Add informative note about tokenization of negative 0') and #9750 ('Clarifying serialization of negative zero') look relevant (titles only; csswg-drafts not readable from this session).

fix.approach: If the maintainer prefers matching WPT/Chromium: in CSSNumber::to_css's zero branch, write `-0` when value.is_sign_negative() (only for token lists, to avoid churning parsed values). Costs one byte in the rare case.

draftReply:
Thanks for the report. The current Editor's Draft of CSS Values 4 says a written `-0` isn't a negative zero: "''0'', ''+0'' and ''-0'' all produce the standard \"unsigned\" zero" (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#calc-ieee). By that text, `calc(1px / -0)` and `calc(1px / 0)` are the same value, so the output is equivalent. You're right that Chromium (and the WPT signed-zero test) treat a literal `-0` as negative, so the spec and implementations disagree here, and there are open CSSWG issues around it. Since this only shows up when dividing by a literal zero, which real stylesheets don't do, I'm going to close this. We can revisit it if the spec settles on signed literals.
